summary: The Cleveland Browns beat the Chicago Bears 20-17 after surviving a game-ending Hail Mary from Justin Fields that nearly fell into Darnell Mooney's hands before being deflected to Browns safety D'Anthony Bell. The Browns rallied from a 17-7 deficit entering the fourth quarter with a field goal, a game-tying touchdown and a go-ahead field goal. The loss dropped Chicago to 5-9 and damaged its playoff hopes, despite a pair of wild-card rivals losing the same weekend.
one_line: Browns beat the Bears 20-17 when a last-second Hail Mary nearly caught by Darnell Mooney was deflected to D'Anthony Bell.
key_facts: The Browns beat the Bears 20-17 after surviving a game-ending Hail Mary.
Justin Fields and the Bears had the ball at the Cleveland 45, trailing by three with five seconds left and no timeouts.
The Hail Mary deflected off Darnell Mooney's hands and legs and into the hands of Browns safety D'Anthony Bell, who made the catch to end the game.
Chicago led 17-7 heading into the fourth quarter, but Cleveland scored a field goal, then a game-tying touchdown with 3:08 left.
Cleveland forced a three-and-out, then drove eight plays for a go-ahead field goal with 32 seconds left, burning all of Chicago's timeouts.
Tyler Scott caught a short pass from Fields and raced 30 yards up the right sideline to the Cleveland 45.
Browns tight end David Njoku said, "I damn near s— myself, dog."
Joe Flacco, in his 16th NFL year, had driven the Browns to the go-ahead score and said you do not get excited until the clock hits zero.
Myles Garrett said he hoped the play would not end up on a YouTube compilation.
Chicago's only touchdowns came after an interception spotted them at the Browns' 1-yard line and on a pick-six, and the offense went three-and-out eight times.
The Bears threw a first-half Hail Mary from the Browns' 37 instead of a 54-yard field goal attempt, resulting in Fields' first interception.
The Bears had won back-to-back games, and the Vikings and Packers also lost, but Chicago fell to 5-9.
